diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the same large table twice (two full sequential scans) and then performs a hash-based deduplication (HASH_GROUP_BY) on the combined ~200k rows, doubling I/O and CPU for scanning and adding a potentially expensive hash aggregation.

hypotheses.claim: UNION forces a deduplicating aggregate over both inputs. (matched: rips where trip_distance > 30 union select pulocationid, payment_type,)

The UNION node concatenates two full table scans on the same table; a single scan with a combined filter (trip_distance > 30 OR fare_amount > 100) followed by a single distinct would read the table once and avoid duplicate work.

Each SEQ_SCAN reads the entire table and applies a filter that returns ~99k rows; the filters are not selective enough to justify two separate scans, and the projected columns are the same in both scans.
